Steve Smith (basketball) played professional basketball.
Steve Smith was born on March 31, 1969.
Steve Smith is an American.
Steve Smith is a former professional basketball player.
Steve Smith is a basketball analyst for Turner Sports.
Steve Smith had a collegiate career with Michigan State.
Steve Smith played several teams in his 14-season National Basketball Association (NBA) career.
Steve Smith played with the Miami Heat, Portland Trail Blazers, San Antonio Spurs, New Orleans Hornets, and Charlotte Bobcats during his NBA career.
Steve Smith is best known for his five-year stint with the Atlanta Hawks which included an All-Star Game appearance in 1998.
Steve Smith won a championship with the San Antonio Spurs in 2003.
Steve Smith was widely regarded as an excellent three-point shooter.
Steve Smith is one of three players to make seven 3-pointers in a quarter.
Steve Smith joined the USA men's national basketball team for the 1994 FIBA World Championship and won a gold medal.
Steve Smith also won another gold medal at the 1999 Tournament of the Americas with the USA men's national basketball team.
Steve Smith won an Olympic gold medal with the USA men's national basketball team at the 2000 Summer Olympics.
Steve Smith finished his four-year career as Michigan State's all-time leading scorer, with 2,263 points.
Steve Smith ranks fourth on Michigan State's all-time assists list (453).
Steve Smith ranks fifth on Michigan State's all-time rebounds list (704).
Steve Smith averaged 18.5 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 3.7 assists per contest during his college career in 122 games.
Steve Smith was named to the NABC All-American First Team as a senior at Michigan State.
Steve Smith led the Spartans to a Big Ten Championship and Sweet Sixteen appearance in 1990.
Steve Smith hit a game-winning, last-second three-pointer against Wisconsin–Green Bay in the first round of the 1991 NCAA Tournament.
Steve Smith was inducted into Michigan State University Athletics Hall of Fame in 2001.
Steve Smith was selected fifth overall in the 1991 NBA draft by the Miami Heat.
Glen Rice, Rony Seikaly, and Brian Shaw were teammates with Steve Smith on the Miami Heat during his rookie season.
Steve Smith played in 61 games in his rookie season for the Miami Heat, starting in 59 with averages of 12 points a game and 4.6 assists.
The Miami Heat made the playoffs to face the top-seeded defending champion Chicago Bulls in Steve Smith's rookie season.
Chicago Bulls swept the Miami Heat in 3 games in the first round during Steve Smith's rookie season.
Steve Smith averaged 16 points a game for the series against the Chicago Bulls in his rookie season.
Injuries limited Steve Smith to 48 games in the 1992–93 season with the Miami Heat, but he increased his scoring average to 16 points a game.
The Miami Heat did not make the playoffs that year.
Steve Smith enjoyed some of the most productive seasons of his career while wearing an Atlanta Hawks uniform.
Steve Smith started in 59 of 78 games for Atlanta and averaged 16 points during the regular season and 19 points in the playoffs with the Atlanta Hawks.
The Atlanta Hawks lost to the Indiana Pacers in a first-round sweep during Steve Smith's time with the team.
Steve Smith led all scorers in Game 4 against the Orlando Magic with 35 points, but Atlanta lost the series 4 games to 1.
Steve Smith averaged 21.7 points in 10 playoff games that postseason with the Atlanta Hawks.
The following season, Steve Smith averaged 20.1 points a game and was named an NBA All-Star as he scored 14 points in 16 minutes of action in the 1998 NBA All-Star Game.

Steve Smith's team, the Atlanta Hawks, disappointed in the playoffs that year, losing to the Charlotte Hornets 3 games to 1 in the conference semifinals despite a 24.8 ppg scoring average by Steve Smith for the series.
The 1998–99 season was limited to 50 games as a result of a league-wide lockout with Steve Smith averaging 18.7 points a game and leading the Hawks to another 5-game first-round victory over Detroit.
Steve Smith averaged 17.3 points in the 1999 playoffs with the Atlanta Hawks.
The Atlanta Hawks traded Steve Smith, Ed Gray, Jim Jackson, and Isaiah Rider to the Portland Trail Blazers for Rasheed Wallace and Scottie Pippen.
Portland was a loaded team that had reached the Western Conference Finals in the 1999 playoffs and featured star forward Rasheed Wallace as well as the newly acquired Scottie Pippen with Steve Smith.
Steve Smith averaged 14.9 points a game in 81 starts for Portland, leading the Trail Blazers to the second-best record in the Western Conference.
Steve Smith increased his scoring average to 17.1 in the playoffs with Portland.
Portland defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves and Utah Jazz before facing the Los Angeles Lakers in the NBA Finals.
The Los Angeles Lakers won Game 5 on the road, then won Game 6 at home as Steve Smith scored 26 points to set up a game 7 matchup against the Lakers.
Despite leading by double digits heading into the fourth quarter, the Lakers came back to win the game and advance to the NBA Finals where they won the NBA Title.

Steve Smith represented the United States at the 2000 Summer Olympics for the USA men's national basketball team and averaged just over 6 points a game in the Olympics including a 12-point performance against China in the group stage of the tournament.

The Trail Blazers entered the 2000–01 season with high expectations but struggled to repeat the success of the previous season due to injuries taking their toll and new additions and trades hurting team chemistry.
Steve Smith only started in 36 of 81 games for Portland, averaging 13.6 points a game during that season.
The Portland Trail Blazers suffered another loss to the Lakers in the playoffs, this time in a three-game sweep in the first round.
Following the season, Steve Smith was traded to the San Antonio Spurs for Derek Anderson and Steve Kerr.
The San Antonio Spurs featured superstars Tim Duncan and David Robinson as they attempted to win another championship.
Steve Smith averaged 11.6 points a game in 76 starts while leading the league in three-point shooting at 47 percent during his time with the San Antonio Spurs.
Steve Smith averaged double figure scoring in the Spurs' first-round win over the Seattle SuperSonics, including 17 points in Game 1 victory.
Steve Smith struggled against the defending champion L.A. Lakers, who defeated the Spurs in 5 games.
The following 2002–03 season marked Steve Smith's final year with San Antonio as he averaged 6.8 points a game and was used sparingly during the playoffs.

The San Antonio Spurs eliminated the Phoenix Suns, three-time champion Lakers, and Dallas Mavericks before defeating the New Jersey Nets in six games to win the NBA title, which was Steve Smith's first and only championship.
Just before the 2003–2004 season started, free agent Steve Smith signed with the New Orleans Hornets.
Steve Smith played in 71 games for the New Orleans Hornets, averaging 5 points a game and shooting 40 percent from beyond the three-point arc.
The New Orleans Hornets made the playoffs but lost to Miami in a grueling back-and-forth series.
Despite losing the final 7th game in Miami, Steve Smith scored 25 points, including 5 three-pointers, against his former team.
Once again a free agent before the following season, Steve Smith signed with the Charlotte Bobcats.
Steve Smith played in 37 games for the Charlotte Bobcats and averaged 7.9 points a game.
At midseason, Steve Smith was traded to Miami for Malik Allen.
Steve Smith was used sparingly by the Heat during their playoff run which concluded with a loss in the conference finals to the defending champion Detroit Pistons.
Following the season, Steve Smith announced his retirement.
Steve Smith worked as an announcer on Atlanta Hawks games with Bob Rathbun and on the Big Ten Network as a college basketball analyst.
For the 2008 season, Steve Smith took a position at NBA TV and was replaced for Hawks broadcasts by Dominique Wilkins.
During the 2011 NBA All-Star Weekend, Steve Smith was a member of the Atlanta team that won the Shooting Stars Competition.
Steve Smith is well known for his charitable pursuits, including a US$2.5 million gift in 1997 to Michigan State University.
The donation helped fund the Clara Bell Smith Student Athlete Academic Center, named after his mother.
This was the largest single donation by a professional athlete to his former school in history.
Steve Smith has a close philanthropic relationship with Children’s Healthcare of Atlanta where he hosts fundraising events for the pediatric hospital.
Steve Smith first met his wife, Millie, at a charity tennis tournament in Detroit.
They had a long-distance relationship for more than a year before getting married in 1996.
The couple have two sons, Brayden and Davis.
Steve Smith often coaches them in soccer and basketball.
Steve Smith is the older cousin of NBA point guard Kay Felder.
Steve Smith resides in Atlanta.
